name: Approval resumed → awaiting_approval→executing (+ clear markers, tool-gate)
description:
ADR-053 Phase 4c PR-2 — the tool-gate RESUME transition. Fires on the RUN entity (agent.chain.execution.<runID>) when the approvalpause subscriber has stamped agent.run.approval-resumed there (in response to agent.approval_response.<loopID>) AND the run is parked in `awaiting_approval`. Advances the run back to `executing` via lifecycle_transition and clears BOTH approval markers, so the run resumes honestly and a future tool-gate can pause again. The 4c twin of clarification-resume rule 11.

WHO STAMPS THE MARKER: like the 4c pause (rule 12), the resume marker is stamped by the product-shell cmd/semteams/approvalpause SUBSCRIBER, not a rule. When the human approves/rejects/modifies via POST /teams-dispatch/loops/{id}/approval, dispatch publishes agent.approval_response.<loopID>; the subscriber graph-reads the loop's run anchor and stamps agent.run.approval-resumed on the run entity. THIS rule is the marker→transition half (mirror of 11). The marker is decision-independent — approve, reject, AND modify all un-park the loop (the framework re-injects the tool result and the loop continues), so all three resume the run.

ORDERED on_enter (bounce-proof): (1) lifecycle_transition awaiting_approval→executing; (2) remove_triple agent.run.approval-pending; (3) remove_triple agent.run.approval-resumed. The ORDER + rule 12's resume-mutual-exclusion guard (agent.run.approval-resumed length_eq 0) make a pause↔resume bounce impossible at EVERY intermediate KV revision, WITHOUT an atomic-write primitive:
  R0 (pre): phase=awaiting_approval, pending set, resumed set — rule 13 matches.
  R1 (after transition): phase=executing, pending set, resumed set — rule 12 blocked (its approval_resumed length_eq 0 guard fails; resumed still set).
  R2 (after remove pending): phase=executing, pending GONE, resumed set — rule 12 blocked (its approval_pending ne "" fails).
  R3 (after remove resumed): phase=executing, both gone — rule 12 blocked (pending gone).
At no revision can rule 12 re-fire, so the run cannot bounce back to awaiting_approval. approval_pending is removed BEFORE approval_resumed precisely so the window between R2 and R3 (resumed-still-set, pending-gone) is also safe.

WHY clear BOTH markers: approval_resumed MUST be cleared or rule 12 stays permanently blocked (the guard) and a SECOND tool-gate could never pause. approval_pending MUST be cleared or rule 12 would re-fire the instant approval_resumed is gone. Both are required for repeated gate→approve cycles to work.

PHASE GUARD IS A TOP-LEVEL CONDITION (agent.run.phase==awaiting_approval), not an action `when` — same discipline as 02/03/04/09/11/12. The awaiting_approval→executing edge is already legal in the upstream transition table (agentrun.go), so no lifecycle change.

DISJOINT FROM 4b-2: this resumes a 4c TOOL-GATE pause (gated on approval_resumed + clears approval_*). The 4b-2 clarification resume (rule 11) is gated on clarification_resumed + clears clarification_*. The two MUST NOT cross-resume — pinned by the agent_run_pack disambiguation contract tests.

on_enter.reason: human approved/rejected the gated tool — run resumed (ADR-053 4c)

metadata.role: tool-gate resume transition (awaiting_approval→executing + marker-clear, run-entity transition)
metadata.marker_stamped_by: cmd/semteams/approvalpause subscriber (consumes agent.approval_response.<loopID>, resolves the run anchor via graph read, stamps agent.run.approval-resumed). No 07/08-analog rule.
metadata.joins_with: 12-executing-to-awaiting-on-approval.json (the pause twin, whose approval_resumed length_eq 0 guard makes this rule bounce-proof) + 11-resume-awaiting-to-executing.json (the 4b-2 clarification resume; disjoint marker).
metadata.fires_on: the run entity (agent.chain.execution.<runID>) — same firing-entity discipline as 02/03/04/09/11/12.
metadata.remove_triple_subject: no subject override → defaults to the firing entity (the run entity), so the run's own markers are cleared.
metadata.ordered_removes_are_load_bearing: transition → remove approval_pending → remove approval_resumed, in THAT order. Combined with rule 12's approval_resumed length_eq 0 guard, every intermediate KV revision keeps rule 12 blocked (resumed-still-set OR pending-gone). No atomic-write primitive needed.
metadata.phase_guard_is_condition: agent.run.phase==awaiting_approval is a TOP-LEVEL CONDITION so the invalid edge is never attempted.
metadata.edge_is_legal_upstream: awaiting_approval→executing is already in the agentrun lifecycle transition table — no upstream change.
metadata.decision_independent: approve, reject, and modify all un-park the loop, so the subscriber stamps approval_resumed for any decision and this rule resumes the run regardless.
metadata.vs_4b2: Disjoint from the 4b-2 clarification resume (rule 11): keyed on approval_resumed, clears approval_* only — never clarification_*. No cross-resume.
metadata.timeout_resume_gap: This run-phase resume is coupled to a PUBLISHED agent.approval_response (the human's decision via POST /loops/{id}/approval). The upstream approval-TIMEOUT sweeper (approval_sweeper.go) un-parks the loop IN-PROCESS without publishing an approval_response, so a timed-out gate would leave the RUN wedged in awaiting_approval while the loop moves on. LATENT today — flow-bootstrap/e2e-flow-bootstrap set no ApprovalTimeout (zero = wait-indefinitely), so the sweeper never fires. An operator who sets a tool-gate timeout re-opens it. Owned by the deferred cancel/timeout reaper slice (ADR-053 §4c cancel), together with the abandoned-clarification timeout; the symmetric upstream fix is to have the sweeper publish its synthetic ApprovalResponse (it already builds the exact payload) — FILED as semstreams#266.
